title: Proposal: global digest-based inline module resolution

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

- Sharing de-duplicated style modules across shadow roots, without having to host the style on a separate URL
- Serializing `adoptedStylesheets` on the server
- importing/export inline scripts

The module map, and specifically the `importmap`, relies on mapping a document-global name to a URL.
This has a few limitations:
- The keys are a global namespace, so writing to it affects the entire document
- The values are URLs, and there is no standard way to map them to an element, specifically inside shadow roots

### What solutions exist today?

Today, the only way to export inline scripts/styles is with putting data URLs in the importmap.
This is very memory inefficient and quite unreadable.

Also, authors need to use a `<script>` tag (and script CSP etc) to share stylesheets across shadow roots.
It feels like sharing styles is not something that would require a script.
Also it doesn't address the global namespace issue. 

Some other suggested solutions like #10673 (using a `specifier` attribute) do the same thing implicitly - allow any script/style element to write into the importmap. #11019 and #10710 explore using `#` and IDrefs for this, but hash fragments don't have a good model across shadow roots, or require drilling down recursively via `referenceTarget` etc.



### How would you solve it?

Suggesting to allow exporting modules (scripts, styles, json, text) to a [content-addressable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content-addressable_storage) URL, as in a URL based on the content it represents.

Effectively, the content would be a blob, but the URL representing it would be (something like) a SHA1 digest of the contents, whether the contents are fetched from outside or inline.

```html
<!-- somewhere -->
<style exportblob="sha1:h0TJuPEXp/P6adSyOua/coEhWrw=">
* { color: red };
</style>

<script exportblob="sha1:8zUcSlLEu1SHzTWZ7tMU9RL2ihI">
export const v = 1;
</script>

<!-- somewhere else, including a different shadow tree -->
<style>
@import "blob:sha1:h0TJuPEXp/P6adSyOua/coEhWrw=";
</style>

<script>
  import {v} from "blob:sha1:8zUcSlLEu1SHzTWZ7tMU9RL2ihI";
</script>
```

Then if the author *does* want to also export this with a well known name, they can still add an `importmap` and export the blob under a shorter global name of their choice. But it's not mandatory for sharing content.

### Anything else?

Some processing model suggestion:
- When either the attribute changes or the inline contents are resolved (end tag), the attribute is checked against the contents
- If they match, a blob is created with the contents, addressable by the special URL
- That blob is imported (added to the module map), and associated with the element
- Removing the element, updating its content, or changing the attribute, revokes the special blob URL
- Updating the stylesheet with CSSOM does not re-check the URL.
